resolution: Third pass on the Surface-mode occlusion overlay: the remaining vanishing edges were on GRAZING panels — at shallow view angles a panel sweeps a huge depth range within a few pixels, so the grid's flat relative eps (0.3% of distance) classified points a hair past a shallow hull fold as occluded and whole visible edges died. Fix: slope-scaled depth bias (the classic wireframe polygon-offset) in occPointHidden — each covering triangle also forgives the depth it sweeps across 2 screen px of its own gradient, computed exactly from the tri's linear 1/z plane. Grazing coverers get large slack (silhouette markers survive), frontal coverers get ~zero (greebles behind the hull stay hidden). Also made pickVertex/pickEdge trust the visibility mask instead of re-running the raw ray occlusion test, so drawn == clickable. New unit test: grazing panel keeps a near-silhouette point the raw ray test calls occluded, while a genuinely buried point stays hidden. 163/163 mesh-edit tests pass. Needs dev-host rebuild to see it.
